architecture.mechanism: Institutional adaptation — a transit system can sustain service regularity under disruptive, demand-varying conditions through adaptive operational rules and technological preparation rather than by expanding capacity (fleet size).
architecture.intervention: Replace fixed-schedule dispatching with adaptive headway management on existing buses: real-time AVL/APC tracking, dynamic holding at control points, and adaptive interlining/turnback rules that re-time the same fleet to equalize gaps as demand fluctuates along the route.
architecture.expected_effect: Headway variance falls and buses self-separate into even intervals, so three-bus bunching followed by 30-minute gaps is eliminated with no added buses.
architecture.falsification_test: Run a 4-week A/B trial on one bunched route (treatment: adaptive headway control; control: fixed schedule, same fleet), logging per-stop arrival times; the mechanism is falsified if headway standard deviation and the fraction of headways below 3 minutes do not decrease by at least 20% on the treatment route versus control.

challenge.kill_reason: all deterministic checks passed; the adversarial gauntlet's objections are ESCALATED (uncalibrated attacker, Art. L) and ride the record for adjudication
